paragraphs.heading: The art of asking questions
paragraphs.edited: But there's a really simple strategy that I want you to add in and to talk about with your students: when they're engaged in a conversation, you want to make sure that you are asking questions. That's what this week is all about — the idea and the art of asking questions. Questions are so, so important. If we ask good questions, then we're probably going to get good answers. Just like any good teacher knows, you don't ask yes-or-no questions. You ask in-depth, probing questions — "why" kinds of questions — to draw out of people the answers that you want, the answers that you need.

paragraphs.heading: The most valuable tool
paragraphs.edited: The most valuable tool that you or your students have is the ability to sit down face-to-face with somebody and have a conversation. There are a lot of tips and tricks to sharing your faith, but the number one thing to keep in your toolbox is the ability to ask great questions and to engage in deep, meaningful conversations with another person. It does so much more than just give the gospel. It builds relationship, so that when that person finally receives Christ, discipleship can actually begin, rather than just a conversion.
